status_definitions.faithful_translation: Checked translation or complete human reconstruction of the cited statement, retaining all explicitly identified input hypotheses.
status_definitions.derived_simplification: A new human proof or extracted numerical consequence corresponding to the cited source statements; not claimed as the named source proof.
status_definitions.remaining_input: A precisely located integral or polynomial construction whose substantive proof is not fully reproduced in this pass.

claims.title: An explicit complementary standard-monomial family
claims.statement: At a selected even twist use arrays e with e(0,0)=nu_0; at a selected odd twist use arrays with zero first row. Deleting respectively the first row/column or first row/last column identifies these with tail-shape arrays. Odd reversal gives lambda^0_2 minus the reversed original tail. Thus n2 is the product of D_(k-1)(tail) on selected twists and D_k(lambda^0) elsewhere.
assumptions: Dominant integral weights and the selected-flat/remainder decomposition of WeightHyp.
Integral monic standard-monomial basis and equality of the interlaced-array count with Weyl dimension are retained inputs.
claims.source_relation: The selected-array bijections and dimension identifications are reconstructed; the whole straightening/basis theorem is not.

claims.title: The exact complementary count supplies the required rank fraction
claims.statement: If selected gaps d_s>=a>0, selected tail spread<=c0 and kc0/a<=1, then (1-kc0/a)^N dimV <= n2 product_s binom(d_s+k-1,k-1). A symbol family of size at least (1-Cr N r^2 k/Y) q^(-r(k-r)) times that product therefore yields bn2>=rho dimV/q^(r(k-r)), with rho the product of the two loss factors.
assumptions: The selected gap/spread inequalities stated in the claim.
The distinct saturated symbol family and its separate dimension lower bound.
The nonnegative-factor case and the automatic negative-factor case are distinguished.
claims.source_relation: Includes a short elementary proof of (1-kx)(1+x)^(k-1)<=1. It does not manufacture the separate symbol dimension bound.

claims.title: Every primitive combination remains primitive
claims.statement: For an integral nonzero residual determinant factor P, saturated independent symbols B_b, and compatible lifts subst(F_b)=B_b P, every coefficient array with a unit entry gives sum c_(b,i) Theta(F_b) h_i outside wR_e. Leading exponents recover the flat exponent and complementary array; reduction, independence, polynomial cancellation and saturation then force all coefficients divisible by w if the sum were divisible.
assumptions: P is integral and has nonzero reduction.
The O-span of the B_b is saturated and the B_b are independent.
The standard-monomial basis is integral and monic; the coefficient transport identifies the actual edge lattice with that integral model.
The coefficient array is O-valued and has at least one unit entry.
claims.source_relation: Reconstructs the universal primitive-combination argument, not merely nonzero tests of each displayed generator.

claims.title: A short characteristic-zero operator-word theorem
claims.statement: For H_d=Sym^d(F^k) in characteristic zero, an adjoint-stable subspace W of End(H_d) spanned by diagonal-weight vectors with all coordinates <=c lies in the span of words of length<=c in X_a partial_b. Highest vectors in End(H_d) are exactly X_1^j Y_k^j (sum X_iY_i)^(d-j). Complete reducibility gives one summand for each j. Applying the Fock commutator and row-degree bound puts every remainder contraction in c0-word closure, factor by factor.
assumptions: F has characteristic zero.
W is commutator-stable and spanned by simultaneous diagonal-weight vectors.
Standard characteristic-zero complete reducibility of finite-dimensional rational GL_k representations.
For the application, the remainder representation is spanned by bideterminants of width<=c0 and the Fock restriction is nondegenerate.
claims.source_relation: New human proof via localization and highest weights; the source uses a different quadric-vanishing implementation. Neither integral coefficients of words nor integral semisimplicity are claimed. Lie stability plus torus weights is explicitly converted to GL stability before complete reducibility.

claims.title: Contractions detect primitive vectors and transfer their dual tests
claims.statement: Assume p^kappa_i Rbar_i <= Psi_i(R_i prime) <= Rbar_i, perfect normalized pairings and the corresponding vertex comparisons. Cartan multiplication and Lambda_beta=p^kappa0 Psi_0^(-1) M_beta Psi_f yield integral contractions. If every contraction lies in w^(2kappa+1)R_f, perfectness gives u in wR_0. For primitive u select rho u=w^nu y with 0<=nu<=2kappa; the normalized adjoint Lambda=p^(-Arem)rho* has height loss ell=rNc0+2rnPrime cpp and c=w^(2kappa-nu) satisfies c beta_0(u,Lambda T)=p^kappa beta_f(y,T).
assumptions: O is the source DVR, w is its uniformizer and w^2=p.
Finite free full source, remainder and flat lattices with their stated perfect pairings.
The integral Weyl/Fock sandwich and vertex comparisons, retained as CL12.
Cartan spanning and actual coordinate/tensor identifications.
The nonselected factors have spread<=2cpp and may be contracted against an integral dual basis.
claims.source_relation: The primitive detection, scalar normalization and nonunit-c transfer are proved. Nonselected twists are peeled without increasing kappa; they contribute to the height loss. No positivity of the signed determinant weight Arem is assumed.

claims.title: The selected lattice comparison exponents cost at most four L
claims.statement: For i=0,f, kappa_i=sum over selected positive spreads h_(i,s) of binom(k,2) floor(log_p(h_(i,s)+k-1)). Under h_(i,s)+k<=a^2, each kappa_i<=2Nk^2 log_p a, hence kappa<=4L, L=Nk^2 log_p a.
assumptions: The explicit Weyl/Fock comparison exponent from CL12.
The numerical consequences h+k<=a^2, p>1 and a>=p of the full Type-II hypotheses.
claims.source_relation: The source restSize witness is CK=4. These exponents measure integral lattice comparison, not representation dimension.

claims.title: Normalized Fock integrality follows from factorial valuations
claims.statement: For integral multihomogeneous G,H of degree d, p^kappa_fl <G,H>/f is integral, with f=product d_s! and kappa_fl=sum k floor(log_p d_s), using Nat.log_p(0)=0. Legendre factorial valuations bound the relevant multinomial coefficient valuations. In all later formulas v(p)=1 and v(w)=1/2.
assumptions: Integral polynomial coefficients, the coefficient Fock pairing and fixed multidegrees.
The source valuation on the fraction field extends p-adic valuation with v(p)=1.
claims.source_relation: The source identifier twiceValuationFactorialProduct equals padicValNat p(product d_s!), with no extra factor two; the report makes this normalization explicit.

claims.title: Joint projection selection and factorial cancellation cost nine L
claims.statement: A finite complete family of commuting projectors has a component with weighted coefficient valuation no larger than the original, by the ultrametric inequality. Successive selections add no extra loss. The explicit normal denominators satisfy Dno<=6L and factorial deficits complete the cost <=9L. In PickCore, k0=C cY nu! z then satisfies v(k0)<=v(f)-n0+9L by cancellation of the selected normal and plane factorial terms.
assumptions: The actual nested/disjoint normal cuts, their commuting complete Fock-selfadjoint projectors, and individual integral denominators.
NoAt and GaAt, including the precise normal approximation scalar and digit-factorial unit corrections, are retained.
The numeric cut-count, total-degree and size inequalities recorded in report sections 1 and 6.
claims.source_relation: Reconstructs the greedy selection and scalar/factorial bookkeeping; it does not claim to construct the isotypic projectors or normal approximation polynomial. The source sizeStep witness is CDn=9.

claims.title: The flat Gram value divides p to the ceiling of forty-nine L
claims.statement: Given the structured signed-chain test outputs, <G,H>=M+E with v(M)<=v(f)+29L and v(E)>=cP-20L+v(f)-kappa_fl. Since kappa_fl<=20L and cP>69L, the error has strictly larger valuation. The integral normalized value y therefore divides p^DX, DX=ceil(49L)<=50L for L>=1.
assumptions: The constrained test, membership, normal approximation and Gram outputs listed in report section 9.
The frame-chain estimate Dm+Dl+3kp<=20L; this geometric estimate remains an input.
kappa_fl<=20L, L>=1 and the strict depth bound cP>69L.
claims.source_relation: The formal witnesses are CDn=9 and CDm=20, giving CDf=CDn+2CDm+1=50. The value_core and divisor deductions are reconstructed, while the structured polynomial test is explicitly retained.

claims.title: Realization errors preserve the divisor bound and the scalar transfer is integral
claims.statement: If y divides p^DX and 2DX<cP, then y+w^cP z still divides p^DX: after multiplying by a divisor witness, the new factor is 1+w^(cP-2DX)zb and hence a unit. RealAt applies this to the finite symbol realization of H. If c x=p^kappa yprime with c integral and yprime dividing p^DX, then x divides p^(kappa+DX), without requiring c to be a unit.
assumptions: The integral realization RealAt, supplied by the companion localizer construction, and the exact symbol membership MembAt.
The valuation depth inequalities, integrality of the full dual value and the loss ell in CL5.
The finite dual-test sum preserves the required height and off-edge support bounds.
claims.source_relation: The perturbation and scalar transfer are complete elementary proofs. No denominator is introduced by dividing by the generally nonunit c.

claims.title: An explicit Type-II denominator constant fifty-four
claims.statement: Combining the pinned witness choices gives D1=kappa+DX<=54Nk^2 log_p a for every primitive coefficient array. The dual test has t_T<=t0+Nc0+ell and lies in w^cStar times every other incoming-edge dual lattice, with cP=cStar+ell. This is valid after enlarging the source sufficiently-large-C threshold to dominate all retained construction thresholds and 54.
assumptions: All exact source Type-II, frame, orbit, weight, lattice and large-C hypotheses; representative consequences are listed in report section 1.
Dp>=C L and cStar>=8(Dp+1), with C sufficiently large for every retained construction.
All explicit retained inputs in CL12.
claims.source_relation: 54=4+9+2*20+1 is extracted from actual witness choices, not asserted as a pre-existing named Lean constant or as a sufficient threshold for every other hypothesis.

claims.title: Exact unresolved integral and constrained-polynomial inputs
claims.statement: This reconstruction retains (i) integral monic standard monomials and their count; (ii) the explicit normalized Fock Weyl/costandard sandwich; (iii) MemAt for the c0-word closure, commuting normal projectors, GaAt, NoAt and ProjectionDerivativeEstimate(26,2,24,60), including exact XX/YY and frame-chain constraints; (iv) MembAt and the companion symbol/path-generator dimension input. These are precise proved-source dependencies whose substantive constructions are not all reproduced here.
assumptions: The exact source hypotheses and quantifier order, not just the numerical summary in this note.
claims.source_relation: Remaining_input denotes a boundary of the human reconstruction, not an axiom or hole in Lean. Characteristic-zero complete reducibility in CL4 does not replace the integral sandwich in this claim. The companion SY and EL sections own their separate improvements.
